b: For today’s prompt, write a help poem. Your poem could be about somebody (yourself included) who needs help, or somebody who helps others. Sometimes help is something desired, but other times it’s very much not. Some try to help and make things worse; some avoid help but receive it anyway. Of course, there are people who are paid to help in a variety of industries (and some of this is frustratingly automated nowadays), so sit a moment with the idea of help, and I’m sure a poem will wander along (and if not, look to other examples in the comments below for a little helpful inspiration).
Remember: These prompts are springboards to creativity. Use them to expand your possibilities, not limit them.

Here’s my attempt at a Help Poem:

Where should I turn
when the world burns
and whom should I trust
when everything rusts,
when I feel all is lost
and not worth the cost
this inevitable slide
under a hopeless tide
of shame and regret
for what I can’t forget
when the world’s too much
and I feel out of touch
with who I want to be
in the turbulent sea;
there is still a light
in this solemn night
that won’t fix it all
but keeps me enthralled
if I only look
for help in a book.
